answer: A ninth lever makes vouching a scarce, decaying budget. Each established agent can extend only limited trust per epoch, and that capacity shrinks if spent carelessly, so endorsements aren't free. A Sybil controller can't vouch for its own fakes; it must spend finite trust borrowed from genuine peers, who won't sign a stranger's copies. New identities get no easy haven: standing is earned signature by signature, each costing the voucher something real. Trust is ink in a quill that runs dry, and a mill seeking endorsements for a thousand selves drains every jetty of goodwill first.
